neighbours.label: verb after a generic second-person 'you' addressing the reader (you know, you have to admit, you may want)
fire: When you live by the sea, you know that storms can come quickly.
Let's be honest: you have to admit, the new design looks much better.
If you've ever moved house, you know how tiring it can be.
Before buying a used car, you might want to check its history.
Honestly, you must admit the ending was a surprise.
When you travel a lot, you learn to pack light.
If you are new to running, you may want to start slowly.
Once you've tasted fresh bread, you know the difference.
quiet: When she lived by the sea, she knew that storms could come quickly.
Let's be honest: the critics had to concede the new design looked much better.
If he has ever moved house, he knows how tiring it can be.
Before buying a used car, my brother checked its history.
Honestly, the critics agreed the ending was a surprise.
When they travel a lot, they pack light.
If Maria is new to running, she plans to start slowly.
Once the baker tasted fresh bread, he noticed the difference.

predictions: Fires on know/admit/want/learn after reader-addressed 'you'; quiet when the same clause has he/she/they or a named person.
notes: Card: ' you' x6, want x4, admit x2, know, think. Probes: 'you know that' 0.616, 'You have to admit' 0.460, 'you think' 0.192, 'might want to' 0.255; third-person versions 0.019-0.064, 'I think' 0.002.
